subject: science
passage: The mirror test, in which an animal is marked in a spot it can see only in a mirror, has long served as a measure of self-recognition; passing it, by touching or inspecting the mark, has been convincingly documented in only a handful of species, such as great apes. In a 2019 study, researchers reported that cleaner wrasses, small reef fish, scraped marks on their throats against the seafloor after viewing themselves in a mirror. The result divided scientists. Some saw evidence that self-recognition is more widespread than assumed; others argued that the test itself may be flawed, since a fish that spends its life removing parasites from other fish might respond to a parasite-like mark for reasons unrelated to any sense of self.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that cleaner wrasses recognize themselves in mirrors in the same way that great apes do
choices.B: To describe how cleaner wrasses remove parasites from the bodies of other fish on coral reefs
choices.C: To explain why scientists have now abandoned the mirror test as a reliable measure of self-recognition
choices.D: To report a finding that raised questions about animals' abilities and the method used to test them

explanation.why: The text explains the mirror test, reports the 2019 wrasse result, and then says it "divided scientists." One side reads it as evidence about animal self-recognition; the other questions whether "the test itself may be flawed." The text's purpose is to present the finding and the two kinds of questions it raised.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text presents this as only one side of a disagreement; it does not take that position itself.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The wrasses' cleaning behavior is mentioned only to explain one group's doubt about the test.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Some scientists argued the test "may be flawed," but the text never says it has been abandoned.
explanation.D: Correct. The finding led some to rethink which animals recognize themselves and others to doubt the test itself.
